master_narrator.agency_handoff_prompt:
Kenna walked the halls of the sleeping quarters, checking the bio-monitors. It was 0300 hours, yet half the family was awake. The storm had passed, but the static remained. It clung to the Enclave like a second skin. She needed to decouple pineal melatonin suppression and serotonin receptor static caused by post-storm Schumann resonance anomalies using psychoactive Lyceum bryophytes and zero-dust flotation. The sheer volume of static interference made her head throb, a literal physical pressure against her temples.

She found Silas scrubbing the floor, his eyes wild with exhaustion. He was trying to push back against the chaos by imposing order on the dirt. Kenna knelt beside him. She crushed a piece of psychoactive moss, intending to show him it was safe, hoping the action would divert his attention and break his loop. She could hide the remaining dust to appease his hyper-orderly state.

Suddenly, her Vex Override kicked in. The warm, empathetic caretaker vanished, replaced by a hyper-clinical, detached observer. She stopped seeing Silas as a frightened friend and started seeing him as a biological system experiencing a 0.4-hertz limbic stress tremor. She didn't feel the static anymore; she merely quantified its effect on her own neural pathways.

"Affective telemetry logged," she muttered flatly, her voice devoid of inflection. She stood up, her movements precise and unhurried. "Silas. The floor is structurally sound. You require a sensory attenuation tank to reset your cortical rhythms. Zero gravity. Zero dust."

Silas looked up, blinking rapidly, the brush hovering over the metal. "Zero dust?"

"Absolute zero," Kenna replied, turning on her heel. "Elias is waiting. Proceed to the Lyceum."
